ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, A is at the lower left corner, B is at the upper left corner, C is at the upper right corner, and D is at the lower right corner. Point M is on the left side AB, and point N is on the bottom side AD. From vertex C, draw line segments CM and CN respectively, dividing the square into three regions, of which the upper region is triangle BMC. Reasoning: The side length of the square is 3, so the area is 9. Line segments CM and CN divide the area of the square into three equal parts, so the area of each part is 3. The base BC of triangle BMC is the upper side of the square, with length 3; because M is on AB, the height of triangle BMC relative to base BC is BM. Thus (1/2)·3·BM = 3, obtaining BM = 2. Line segment CM connects C to M, the horizontal distance is 3, and the vertical distance is BM=2, so CM = sqrt(3^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(13).

raw_record.question_text: Square $ABCD$ has sides of length 3. Segments $CM$ and $CN$ divide the square's area into three equal parts. How long is segment $CM$?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a square with A bottom-left, B top-left, C top-right, D bottom-right; M lies on the left side AB and segment CM forms the upper-left triangular region BMC. From the text, the square side is 3, so its area is 9, and the two drawn segments divide it into three equal areas of 3 each. Use the upper region triangle BMC: its base BC is the full top side of length 3, and its height is BM along the left side. Set (1/2)(3)(BM)=3 to get BM=2, hence AM=1. Then compute CM as the hypotenuse between C and M: horizontal distance 3 and vertical distance 2, so CM=sqrt(3^2+2^2)=sqrt(13).
